claims: The Apollo 11 mission landed humans on the moon on July 20, 1969.
Apollo missions landed humans on the moon five more times through 1972.
Over 800 pounds of lunar samples have been analyzed by scientists worldwide.
Lunar samples are entirely unique to the lunar environment.
NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter has photographed the Apollo landing sites.
NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter photographs of the landing sites show the lunar modules.
NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter photographs of the landing sites show equipment.
NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter photographs of the landing sites show astronaut tracks.
The Soviet Union tracked the Apollo missions.
Independent observatories have used the laser reflectors placed on the moon to measure the distance to Earth.
Roughly 400,000 people worked on the Apollo projects.
The moon landing flag was held up by a horizontal rod to keep it extended in the vacuum of space.
The moon landing flag appeared wrinkled.
The moon landing flag moved only when astronauts handled it.
Apollo mission cameras were set to take photos of the bright lunar surface in daylight.
Apollo mission cameras could not capture faint stars in the background.
Non-parallel shadows were caused by the uneven, highly reflective lunar surface.
Apollo astronauts passed through the Van Allen belts quickly.
Passing through the Van Allen belts quickly minimized astronauts' radiation exposure
